newsitem.title: UK: Blenheim seen ideal fit for United.
newsitem.headline: Blenheim seen ideal fit for United.

text.p: British-based exhibitions group Blenheim is regarded as an ideal fit for United News & Media, which was earlier reported to be weighing a takeover bid.
"Blenheim's strength in Europe and France in particular mean it would be a good fit (for United)," said one analyst.
"The exhibitions business is also doing quite well at this stage in the cycle," he added.
United News & Media and Anglo-Dutch group Reed Elsevier have long been seen as suitors for Blenheim.
However, industry sources said on Monday that Reed was no longer believed to be in the running.

Dutch publisher VNU stirred the waters last week when it paid 500p per share to take a 15 percent stake in Blenheim. VNU declined comment on reports on Monday that it was set to increase its stake to 25 percent.
It said last week its 15 percent holding in Blenheim was a strategic long-term investment and it had no intention of making an offer for the whole company unless rival offers emerged.

Its move is certain to have concentrated the mind of United News chief executive Clive Hollick, who is now reported to be weighing a bid of up to 520p per share, valuing Blenheim at some 480 million stg.
Blenheim shares closed 6-1/2p lower at 477 1/2p on Monday.
United News has so far refused to declare its hand.
Analysts say that United News' decision is complicated by the fact it is still reorganising its activities following its merger earlier this year with television and financial services group MAI.
"A bid makes a lot of sense but the timing is not good for United News," said Nick Ward of Credit Lyonnais Laing.
Blenheim, in which French utilities company Generale des Eaux has a 15 percent stake, posted pre-tax profit of 35.6 million stg in 1995 on turnover of 202.5 million.

France was its largest source of revenue, accounting for 37 percent of earnings, followed by 26 percent from the U.S., 20 percent from the UK, 11 percent from Germany and six percent from the rest of the world.
Miller Freeman is the business magazines and exhibitions arm of United News. It operates in the U.S., Europe and Asia but analysts regard the American market as its main strength.
Anthony de Larrinaga of Panmure Gordon said a bid of around five pounds per share would represent an attractive deal for investors in both United and Blenheim.
He said that United was likely to be considering a bid between 480p and 530p per share and noted that the difference between the two levels was only around 46 million stg.
